findings.location: <harness-onion>/scripts/evolution_surface.py _gate_link (the own-path test); README 'Programme paths', first bullet of the link rule and the G1R3-2 disposition row ('mirroring the target half')
findings.finding: The own-path half compares the link's on-disk name with the record's entries by spelling (_matches, and startswith for directories that hold gate material), while the target half is judged by identity 'so a case-insensitive file system is covered'. On a case-insensitive file system (the macOS default; the scratch volume is one) a link whose own path differs from a gate path or gate directory only in case stands in place of it, and check_coverage passes with _gate_link False (probe 2): docs/Harnesses -> ../task-packets/p (reading docs/harnesses/x.yaml returns the data file); scripts/Evolution_Surface.py -> other.py (reading scripts/evolution_surface.py returns the data file); docs/Alpha-2 -> ../task-packets/p; architecture/Evolution-Surface-Authority.json -> ../docs/data.md (reading the gate exact path architecture/evolution-surface-authority.json returns the data file). Where the gate entry has files, such a tree needs them gone, so the PR deletes gate paths and pr_approvers gives [OWNER] (scripts/Evolution_Surface.py with scripts/evolution_surface.py: [OWNER]). But architecture/evolution-surface-authority.json has no file at the subject commit (probe 4), so a PR adding only the case-variant link gets [LANE_MONITOR, OWNER] and passes the coverage check: the backstop G1R3-2 relied on is already missing for that entry. Round 2 judged the own path unaffected because it comes from the walk's on-disk names; the name is right, but its comparison with the record is by spelling. Outside this round's scope and not graded: classification itself is case-sensitive, so a regular file at architecture/Evolution-Surface-Authority.json resolves to CONTRACT_AND_SOURCE, passes check_coverage and is what the gate path reads on such a file system (probe 3); a fix in the link rule alone does not close that case. The subject tree has no case-fold collision among its paths or directories and no data path that case-folds onto a gate entry (probe 4), so a case-insensitive rule would refuse nothing in today's tree.
findings.requiredChange: Judge the own-path half without regard to case, as the target half is: for example refuse a link whose case-folded own path equals a case-folded gate entry, lies inside a case-folded gate prefix, or is a case-folded ancestor directory of a gate entry (conservative on case-sensitive systems too); or locate each gate entry in the tree by its recorded spelling and refuse when any component on that route is a symbolic link. Say so in the README, and add tests for docs/Harnesses and architecture/Evolution-Surface-Authority.json as links to data. Separately, consider asking the owner whether the coverage check should refuse any path that equals, or lies under, a gate entry after case folding without matching it exactly.

findings.finding: (a) Descending the any-depth skip directories exposes the fail-closed entry check to bytecode writers. The standard library writes bytecode by creating a temporary file in __pycache__ and renaming it; an entry listed by the walk and renamed before its lstat is refused as COVERAGE. Probe 2: with a thread repeating that create-and-rename in ci/__pycache__, 17 of 324 check_coverage runs on the same tree were refused. Before this change real skip directories were pruned, so such writes were never examined. The same race exists in any walked directory since 1d517f1e (14 of 316 runs with the writer in docs/cache), but there the writer would itself be a fault (E3-8 (c)), while bytecode in __pycache__ is the expected byproduct the skip set exists for. The candidate's checkout test and the oracle's (its line 1582) walk the checkout while the parallel suite's other workers may be importing modules; ci/run_packet_argv.py passes PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE through only when the outer environment sets it, so whether the verify writes bytecode into the checkout is an environment fact for the dry run. (b) A linked root spelled with a trailing separator, or with a final '/.', is accepted and its target walked (probe 2), though the README says a linked root is refused: os.path.islink resolves the link for such a spelling. The candidate test passes a Path, which drops the separator. No gate effect: the target directory is walked and judged as the tree.
findings.requiredChange: Optional. (a) Confirm in the dry run that no bytecode is written into the checkout during the verify, or treat an entry that vanished (ENOENT) inside an any-depth skip directory as absent, keeping every other failure fail-closed. (b) Test the normalized root (os.path.islink(os.path.normpath(root))), or say that the refusal concerns the root's own spelling.
